name: Power-Up Grant
description: The acquirable mutation: double jump, wall cling, dash — new verbs delivered as parameter overrides on the movement components the player already has, never as parallel implementations. A double jump is movement.jump_core with maxJumps raised to 2; building a second jump component would split the forgiveness windows, the event stream, and every downstream count in two. This component owns exactly the grant transaction: marking a powerId as held and applying its declared overrides to named sibling inputs. It deliberately does not own the pickup fantasy (presentation handles the fanfare), does not own gating (world.ability_gate checks what this grants), and does not own persistence — persistence.save_system records progression.power_up_granted like any other durable fact. Because overrides are data, a designer can ship a new power by writing one grant entry and one gate requirement, touching no movement code.

inputs.name: powerId
inputs.description: Stable identifier for this power — the same string world.ability_gate lists in requiredPowerIds. One id, one mutation, one check.

inputs.name: targetOverrides
inputs.description: Entries of {component, input, value} applied on grant — e.g. {movement.jump_core, maxJumps, 2}. The grant composes existing verbs; it never shadows them with new logic.

inputs.name: grantOn
inputs.description: touch grants on contact (classic pickup pedestal); interact requires a deliberate press, which suits upgrades with a ceremony or a choice attached.

inputs.name: uniqueGrant
inputs.description: Whether holding the power already makes the pickup inert. True for permanent abilities; false only for repeatable boosts, which arguably belong to economy instead.

outputs.name: grantedPowerIds
outputs.description: Every power the player holds. This array is the player's capability fingerprint — the thing gates, maps, and save files all read.
